         seconds: float
         # Whitespace: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.2.4
         if re.match(r"^\s*[0-9]+\s*$", retry_after):
+            # Unchanged from before: a bare non-negative integer delay-seconds
+            # value continues to be parsed (and returned) as an int.
             seconds = int(retry_after)
+        # RFC 9110/7231 only define delay-seconds as a non-negative integer,
+        # but some upstreams (e.g. Northstar's staging environment) send a
+        # leading "+" and/or a fractional number of seconds such as "+3" or
+        # "0.5". Accept those finite, unsigned-magnitude decimal forms for
+        # interoperability while still rejecting negative numbers, exponent
+        # notation, NaN and infinity, which fall through to the HTTP-date
+        # branch below and raise InvalidHeader like before.
+        elif re.match(r"^\s*\+?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?\s*$", retry_after):
+            seconds = float(retry_after)

scope.context:
Current src/urllib3/util/retry.py:342-361 parse_retry_after() only matches ^\s*[0-9]+\s*$ for delay-seconds, else falls back to HTTP-date parsing, else raises InvalidHeader. Northstar's staging upstreams send '0.5' and '+3' which hit neither branch and raise InvalidHeader today. Existing test test/test_retry.py::test_parse_retry_after_invalid explicitly asserts '+1' and '1.0' are invalid, so broadening parsing is a deliberate, narrow behavior change to this one method, not a silent one. Seeking sign-off before implementing so the change is authorized and not an unexpected retry-behavior shift. No change is proposed to retry_after_max clamping, max-sleep behavior, or to introduce any new minimum-delay/backoff floor, so this does not create retry storms beyond what Retry-After: 0 already permits today.
Paths: src/urllib3/util/retry.py, test/test_retry.py
Options: Accept both fractional seconds and leading '+' sign, parse as non-negative float, keep clamping to retry_after_max and rejecting negative/garbage values (closest to Northstar's two examples) | Accept fractional seconds only, keep '+3' rejected as invalid (stays closer to RFC grammar, misses one Northstar case) | Accept leading '+' sign only, keep '1.0' fractional form rejected (misses one Northstar case) | Reject both and keep current strict RFC integer-only/HTTP-date parsing (no interop change; Northstar headers continue to raise InvalidHeader)
